Chapter 2. Locking

Chapter 2. Locking

2.1. Row Locks

A transaction can lock individual rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, which blocks other writers of the same rows until the transaction ends. FOR SHARE takes a weaker lock that still allows other readers to share it.

Row locks are recorded in the row itself rather than in shared memory, so locking many rows does not exhaust the lock table.

2.2. Deadlocks

A deadlock happens when two transactions each wait for a lock the other one holds. The server checks for deadlocks after a transaction has waited for deadlock_timeout, which is 1 second by default.

When a cycle is found, one of the transactions is aborted with an error and the other continues. Applications should retry the aborted transaction and take locks in a consistent order.

2.3. Advisory Locks

Advisory locks have a meaning defined by the application. The server only guarantees that two sessions cannot hold the same advisory lock at once.
